html:
Under King Bayinnaung, who reigned from 1550 to 1581, the Taungoo dynasty built the largest empire in the history of Southeast Asia, ruling from Pegu.

He conquered the Shan states, Lan Na, and took Ayutthaya in 1564 and again in 1569, making Siam a vassal. He also took Vientiane from Setthathirath. Portuguese mercenaries served in his armies.

His empire did not long survive him: Siam broke free under Naresuan in 1584, and Pegu fell to rivals in 1599. But Bayinnaung set the pattern of Burmese wars with Siam for two centuries, and is a national hero in Burma. See Hanthawaddy.
sum: Under King Bayinnaung, who reigned from 1550 to 1581, the Taungoo dynasty built the largest empire in the history of Southeast Asia, ruling from Pegu.
